title.narrative: Output 3.3. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative: 1. Waste workers’ formalization: Iterant waste workers are organised by union; then inducted into recycling cooperative; and then integrated in the municipal government’s waste management system for door to door waste collection (Pune) & maintaining municipality’s material recovery facilities (Ahmedabad). (13129 women; 129 men unionized). 2. Moving up the waste value chain: Trained waste workers set up collective scrap shop in Pune and Value Creation Centre (for aggregation & mechanized sorting) in Ahmedabad. 3. Proving the feasibility of green jobs in decentralized waste to wealth initiatives (bio methanation and composting): through feasibility study and pilot how bio digestors can operate within the premises of government/ government funded institutions and homes of waste recyclers (Pilot demonstration in PMC, Indian Institute of Science, Education and Research (IISER) and home of a waste recycler) managed by women workers. 4. Promoting OSH: At 3 levels - Policy research and dialogue; institutional strengthening through training the municipality employees; & building capacities of WOs/EBMOs. 5. Helped almost 10 chemical and pharmaceutical companies build a greener vision. 6. As part of PAGE Work Package 1, Completed Green Jobs Policy Readiness Assessment in India, an undertaking with a focus on the energy sector, to map the policy ecosystem that enables green job creation and Just Transition planning in the country at a macro level. Supplementing this assessment is a regional case study which demonstrates possibility of a Just Energy Transition through industrial and economic diversification in Jharkhand. 7. As part of PAGE Work Package 7, two activities were completed (i) preliminary desk review to identify scope for green job creation through rural development schemes and programmes and (ii) compilation of set of 25 case studies in green rural development, with particular focus on projects/programmes that create/have the scope to create green and decent jobs. Research activities undertaken as part of Just Transition Toolkit 1) Green Jobs in Waste Value Chain: A diagnostic study of Pune and Ahmedabad 2)Practical Policy Brief to establish a city scale system for safe and sustainable management of Domestic Hazardous, Chemical and Biomedical Waste 3)Policy brief on identification and integration waste workers 4)Policy brief on integrating OSH in city scale waste management system 5)Policy Brief on green job creation in waste to wealth initiatives 6)Strategy note for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs on green and decent jobs in waste value chains. Roadmap of action with Pune Municipal Corporation and action plan with the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation; Training of Trainer Workshop on OSH for Employers, workers and Government. With active contribution from RBSA-funded intervention, the ILO launched, as part of Work Package 1 Green Jobs Policy Readiness Assessment in India in 2022, an undertaking with a focus on the energy sector, to map the policy ecosystem that enables green job creation and Just Transition planning in country at macro level. Supplementing this assessment is regional case study that demonstrates possibility of Just Energy Transition through industrial and economic diversification in Jharkhand. These studies were validated in tripartite workshop in June 2023 and have subsequently completed. ILO also initiated work under Work Package 7 to mainstream principles of environmental sustainability in rural development by undertaking preliminary desk review to identify scope for green job creation through rural development schemes implemented by Ministry of Rural Development and through compilation of 25 case studies in green rural development. All activities under PAGE contribute significantly to ILO’s efforts to promote delivery and implementation of policies encouraging green jobs and just transitions in India, as informed by the ILO’s Just Transition guidelines and R204.

description.narrative: Based on the capacity development and knowledge sharing on Quality Apprenticeships, the constituents are able to work towards modernization and transformation of apprenticeships; encourage apprenticeships in MSME; and promote South-South Triangular Cooperation (SSTC) through action plan. The ILO produced a total of 10 reports, including seven global thematic reports and three country reports including the one focused on India in March 2023. These reports have informed innovative ideas and policy options to modernise and transform work-based learning and apprenticeships, based on the extensive review and research on lessons learned and success stories, both at global and country level. As for the India country report, an Innovation Bootcamp was held in April 2022 to share the preliminary findings and capture further insights and experiences from over 120 tripartite constituents and wider stakeholders in the country. The report was then finalized and issued in March 2023 and then launched at the ILO seminar “Sharing good practices and lessons learned in apprenticeships from ADULT project: Way forward based on the new ILO recommendation on Quality Apprenticeships” in August 2023. Based on a request from the Ministry of Skills Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) another study “Promoting and strengthening apprenticeships in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in India” has also been undertaken. Under the South-South Triangular Cooperation (SSTC) project on Quality Apprenticeships in India, South Africa, China, Ethiopia, and Switzerland, the ILO organized the high-level policy dialogue and capacity-building workshop in South Africa as well as two virtual workshops for peer-to-peer learning in 2023. The tripartite participants from the countries participated and actively exchanged insights and experiences on the topic.

description.narrative: Informed solutions by the Government of India to bridge the digital divide in skills development in the country. ILO with funding from Belgium has conducted a feasibility study on the Development and Pilot implementation of the ILO-UNICEF Youth Career Platform in India, The study has looked into the following aspects, among others: (i) Adjustment of the tool to respond to the local needs by looking at potential complementarities and overlaps with the existing local tools; (ii) Adjustment of the tool to respond to context diversity, particularly in what concerns informal environments; (iii) What challenges will it face to be implemented as well as how could it be pilot tested and generalized; (iv) Determine stakeholders’ engagement and willingness to participate in this endeavor; (v) Identifying/mapping pre-existing tools that can be leveraged or built upon; and (vi) Challenges faced by existing platforms in scaling up and taking it to the masses. In partnership with UNICEF/YuWaah, the ILO has launched the Skills Innovation Challenge Call in India with a theme of “upgrading informal apprenticeships through digital transformation” in July 2023. It calls for proposals from not-for-profit organizations in the country that have innovative solutions to address the challenge, with a particular focus on women and girls. Following the evaluation process scheduled, top four winning organizations are selected to receive financial award and technical guidance from the ILO to implement the proposed initiative on the ground.
